This causes abnormal catecholamine biosynthesis, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, and progressive neurodevelopmental injury with seizures, hypotonia, and brain atrophy.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals manifest low copper and ceruloplasmin levels in plasma or serum, as well as in cerebrospinal fluid.
evidence.explanation: Supports systemic copper and ceruloplasmin deficiency as a core biochemical state downstream of ATP7A dysfunction.

steps/5.description: Failed ATP7A-dependent epithelial copper export causes low circulating copper and ceruloplasmin. Systemic copper deficiency limits copper delivery to secretory-pathway cuproenzymes in peripheral tissues.

evidence.snippet: Progressive neurodegeneration and connective tissue disturbances, together with the peculiar 'kinky' hair are the main manifestations.
evidence.explanation: Supports kinky hair as a core Menkes manifestation downstream of copper-transport disruption.

evidence.snippet: Copper is supplied to melanosomes by ATP7A
evidence.explanation: Establishes that ATP7A supplies the copper that activates the pigment-cell cuproenzyme tyrosinase in melanosomes, grounding the reduced tyrosinase-activity and melanin-biosynthesis annotations for the hypopigmentation branch.

steps/6.description: Copper-dependent hair and pigment biology is disrupted, producing brittle twisted hair shafts and hair hypopigmentation. Reduced activity of the copper-dependent enzyme tyrosinase impairs melanin biosynthesis, while defective disulfide cross-linking weakens the keratinized hair shaft.

evidence.snippet: This feature and other connective tissue abnormalities appear to be consequences of deficient activity of lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme.
evidence.explanation: Directly links connective-tissue manifestations in Menkes disease to lysyl oxidase deficiency.

steps/7.description: Copper deficiency reduces lysyl oxidase activity, weakening collagen and elastin cross-linking in connective tissues and vessel walls. This produces tissue laxity, vascular tortuosity and phlebectasia, hernias, and skeletal fragility.

evidence.snippet: We previously identified internal jugular vein phlebectasia (IJP) in four Menkes disease subjects. This feature and other connective tissue abnormalities appear to be consequences of deficient activity of lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme.
evidence.explanation: Supports vascular phlebectasia as a downstream vascular-wall manifestation of lysyl oxidase deficiency.

steps/8.description: Weak elastin and collagen cross-linking in vessel walls leads to tortuous intracranial arteries and benign internal jugular vein phlebectasia.

evidence.snippet: This feature and other connective tissue abnormalities appear to be consequences of deficient activity of lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme.
evidence.explanation: Supports generalized connective-tissue laxity as a downstream manifestation of lysyl oxidase deficiency.

evidence.snippet: In the affected half-brothers, we identified a hemizygous novel non-synonymous variant of unknown significance in AMMECR1 (c.G530A; p.G177D), a gene residing in the AMME disease locus.
evidence.explanation: The first point mutation in the gene, in the family that separated AMMECR1's contribution from the rest of the AMME deletion.

evidence.snippet: These original cases further confirm that most specific AMME features are ascribed to AMMECR1 haploinsufficiency.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation from the deletion side that this gene, not its neighbours, carries the non-renal phenotype.

evidence.snippet: AMMECR1 is composed of six exons, shows a ubiquitous 6.5-kb transcript, and codes for a protein with a molecular mass of 35.5 kDa.
evidence.explanation: The gene's basic architecture, from the report that cloned it out of the AMME deletion interval. Graded OTHER because this is molecular cloning and sequence analysis rather than any of the study types the other values name.

steps/1.description:
The initiating lesion. Reported alleles span the range: microdeletions removing AMMECR1 alone or with its immediate neighbours TMEM164 and SNORD96B, nonsense variants, an X-autosome translocation with skewed inactivation of the normal X, and missense changes. AMMECR1 sits in the Xq22.3 interval deleted in AMME, and the disease-defining observation is that variants hitting AMMECR1 while sparing COL4A5 reproduce the non-renal AMME features without Alport syndrome.
The gene encodes a 35.5 kDa protein from six exons with a ubiquitous transcript, conserved from yeast and nematode upward. When it was cloned, its function was unknown; a conserved six-amino-acid domain in exon 2 was noted with function unknown then, and it remains substantially unknown now.

evidence.snippet: AMMECR1 and AMMECR1L proteins dimerize and localize to the nucleus as suggested by their nucleic acid-binding RAGNYA folds.
evidence.explanation: The structural and localisation account of the normal protein. Graded COMPUTATIONAL because the nucleic-acid-binding function is a fold-based prediction, and INDIRECT because it describes the wild-type protein rather than a patient allele.

evidence.snippet: Transfected cell lines with the p.G177D mutation showed aberrant nuclear localisation patterns when compared with the wild type.
evidence.explanation: The only direct functional demonstration for a patient allele: the mutant protein mislocalises within the nucleus in transfected cells.

evidence.snippet: Comparative review of the literature highlights that while previously reported missense variants in AMMECR1 demonstrated altered intranuclear protein distribution and reduced expression in functional assays, clinical evidence supporting pathogenicity of non-truncating variants remains limited.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the intranuclear-distribution finding generalises across the reported missense alleles, and carries the authors' caveat about how thin the clinical evidence for non-truncating variants still is.

evidence.snippet: The expression pattern of mutated AMMECR1 we observed within the nucleus is consistent with the altered protein being targeted for degradation by this system.
evidence.explanation: The authors' proposed route from the missense allele to loss of nuclear function - proteasomal degradation of the mal-folded protein, inferred from the mutant's resemblance to nuclear 20S proteasome staining and from reduced GFP expression. INDIRECT because it is an interpretation of a localisation pattern, and the source hedges it throughout ("consistent with", "may therefore be"); no degradation assay was performed. It is recorded on this node rather than as a node of its own, because a separate proteasomal node would give a speculative step the same graph weight as the measured mislocalisation.

steps/2.description:
AMMECR1 and its paralog AMMECR1L dimerize and localize to the nucleus, which their nucleic-acid-binding RAGNYA folds would predict. The one patient allele examined functionally, p.G177D, is not absent from the nucleus but distributed abnormally within it - and the second reported missense allele is described the same way, as altered intranuclear distribution with reduced expression.
What the protein does there is unresolved. The strongest statement its investigators make is that it is potentially involved in cell cycle control, inferred from coexpression rather than from an assay of AMMECR1 itself. This node therefore records a demonstrated molecular abnormality with an undetermined downstream function, which is the honest shape of the evidence.

evidence.snippet: AMMECR1 is coexpressed with genes implicated in cell cycle regulation, five of which were previously associated with growth and bone alterations.
evidence.explanation: The coexpression analysis that generated the hypothesis. COMPUTATIONAL and INDIRECT: it is a transcriptomic association, and the inference to cell-cycle involvement is one step beyond what it measures.

evidence.snippet: Our knockdown of the zebrafish orthologous gene resulted in phenotypes reminiscent of patients' features.
evidence.explanation: The animal evidence that the gene is required for normal development. "Reminiscent" is the authors' word and is not upgraded here.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that AMMECR1 is potentially involved in cell cycle control and linked to a new syndrome with growth, bone, heart, and kidney alterations with or without elliptocytosis.
evidence.explanation: The authors' summary claim, at the strength they state it - "potentially involved" - which is why this node's `mechanism_confidence` is HYPOTHETICAL.

steps/3.description:
The proposed bridge between a nuclear protein of unknown function and a multisystem developmental phenotype. AMMECR1 is coexpressed with genes implicated in cell cycle regulation, five of which already have growth and bone phenotypes of their own, and knocking down the zebrafish orthologue produces features reminiscent of the patients'. That is the entire basis; no cell-cycle measurement has been made in patient material, and the proposal is stated by its authors as a possibility.
Recorded as a node anyway, because the alternative is a graph in which a gene deletion connects directly to seven unrelated clinical findings with nothing in between, which would misrepresent the literature in the opposite direction.

evidence.snippet: The elliptocytosis was not associated with any detectable abnormalities in red cell membrane proteins; red cell membrane stability and rigidity was normal on ektacytometry.
evidence.explanation: The negative result that defines this node: the membrane-skeleton mechanism of hereditary elliptocytosis was looked for in these patients and was not there.

evidence.snippet: Blood films revealed the presence of elliptocytes in the older brother.

steps/4.description: Elliptical red cells on the blood film, sometimes with anaemia. The important thing about this finding is what it is not: in the original AMME family the elliptocytosis was not accompanied by any detectable abnormality of red cell membrane proteins, and membrane stability and rigidity were normal on ektacytometry - the assay that is abnormal in hereditary elliptocytosis. So the shared name with hereditary elliptocytosis is a morphological coincidence, not a shared mechanism, and no mechanism has since been proposed.

It is curated because it is the only candidate intermediate any source offers between AMMECR1 loss and the nephrocalcinosis in the disease name, and because the first-report authors treated it as such: they screened a panel of known idiopathic-hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis genes before concluding that AMMECR1 was the remaining candidate.

evidence.snippet: We sought to discover a genetic cause for two half-brothers presenting with nephrocalcinosis, early speech and language delay and midface hypoplasia with submucous cleft palate and bifid uvula.
evidence.explanation: Nephrocalcinosis as the presenting feature in the first AMMECR1 point-mutation family.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report a patient with a heterozygous de novo AMMECR1 missense variant, NM_015365.3:c.649G>A p.(Val217Met) presenting with clinical features consistent with MFHIEN, including midface hypoplasia, partial hearing impairment, nephrocalcinosis, and elliptocytosis identified on peripheral blood smear.
evidence.explanation: Independent recurrence of nephrocalcinosis with a second missense allele.

evidence.snippet: Nephrocalcinosis, hypercalciuria, cataracts (in proband II(2)), submucous cleft palate and bifid uvula are unique to our study and may be entirely incidental; we do not have sufficient evidence in support of any causal relationship between AMMECR1 and these manifestations.
evidence.explanation: The first-report authors declining to attribute the nephrocalcinosis to AMMECR1 at all. It refutes the causal claim rather than the observation - the finding is real and repeatedly imaged in both half-brothers; what is contested is that AMMECR1 caused it. Recorded because nephrocalcinosis is in the disease name, so a reader would otherwise take the association as settled. Note the sentence's own premise ("unique to our study") is now superseded by the second missense case above.

evidence.snippet: We excluded known genetic causes for nephrocalcinosis and idiopathic hypercalciuria in 12 of 14 genes assessed.
evidence.explanation: A rescued negative result: the alternative monogenic explanations for this patient's renal phenotype were looked for and not found, which is what leaves AMMECR1 standing. INDIRECT because excluding other causes is not evidence that this gene is the cause. The authors qualify it themselves - the two unexcluded genes, PTH and CLDN14, had 45% and 86% coverage on the capture kit, and they decline to call them excluded, noting only that neither is on the X chromosome.

steps/14.description: Calcium deposition in the renal parenchyma. This is the renal finding that belongs to AMMECR1; it is distinct from the Alport nephropathy of the contiguous-gene AMME deletion, which comes from COL4A5 and is not part of this entity.

evidence.snippet: Shortly after birth, proband II(1) was noted to have hypotonia and poor feeding.
evidence.explanation: The onset observation, attributed to the older half-brother.

evidence.snippet: Proband II(1) had significant infantile hypotonia1 and delay in gross motor skills in addition.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own summary of the finding in the discussion. The stray "1" is a reference marker in the source text and is retained so the quote matches the cache exactly.

steps/15.description: Low muscle tone from shortly after birth, with poor feeding and delay in gross motor skills. The first-report authors list hypotonia among the features AMMECR1 loss contributes to, alongside speech and language delay and hearing loss - a stronger attribution than the "may play a role" they use for the nephrocalcinosis and cleft palate.

edges/1.description: Deleting the gene removes the protein outright; the studied missense allele leaves the protein present but abnormally distributed within the nucleus. Both routes converge on the absence of normal nuclear AMMECR1 activity.

edges/2.description: The proposed consequence, and the weakest link in this chain. It rests on AMMECR1's coexpression with cell-cycle genes and on the zebrafish knockdown phenotype, not on any measurement of cell-cycle progression in patient cells.

edges/3.description: Drawn separately from the developmental branch because the original family's red cells were shown *not* to have the membrane defect that ordinarily causes elliptocytosis, so this is not a downstream consequence of any established mechanism. The edge records that the blood phenotype tracks AMMECR1 loss; its intermediates are unknown.

edges/4.description: The facial phenotype that named the syndrome. No mechanism connecting AMMECR1 to midfacial growth has been proposed in any source read here.

edges/5.description: The one phenotype with a tissue-level foothold: AMMECR1 protein is expressed in the human fetal cochlea, so the gene is present where the deficit appears. Expression is not mechanism, and nothing further is claimed.

edges/6.description: Proportionate short stature is one of the most consistent features across reports, and the growth phenotype is what led to the cell-cycle coexpression hypothesis in the first place.

edges/7.description: The "mental retardation" of the original AMME acronym, now attributed to AMMECR1 rather than to COL4A5 or the wider deletion.

edges/8.description: Cardiac abnormalities appear in the five-individual loss-of-function series and are not reported in the earlier families, which is why they are curated as part of the spectrum rather than as a core feature.

edges/9.description: Midline palatal defects - a submucous cleft with bifid uvula in the first point-mutation family, a soft cleft palate in a female carrier - alongside the midface hypoplasia, which is what makes the facial phenotype a midline developmental one rather than isolated retrusion.

edges/10.description: Part of the skeletal component, reported both in affected males and in a carrier female.

edges/11.description:
The renal finding that is *not* Alport syndrome. It was the presenting problem in the first point-mutation family and recurs in the most recent missense case, but its investigators put the attribution no more strongly than that AMMECR1 may play a role in it.
This edge is kept alongside the hypercalciuria route below rather than replaced by it, because the second half-brother's nephrocalcinosis has no reported hypercalciuria at all. Whatever the calcium-handling route explains, it does not explain every reported case.

edges/12.description: Excessive urinary calcium excretion with a normal plasma calcium - so a renal tubular handling problem rather than a systemic hypercalcaemia. It is the only candidate intermediate any source offers for the renal phenotype, and it is why the first-report authors screened a panel of idiopathic-hypercalciuria genes before settling on AMMECR1.

edges/13.description: Hypotonia from shortly after birth in one of the two point-mutation half-brothers, listed by the first-report authors among the features AMMECR1 loss contributes to. Explicitly absent in his half-brother, who met his motor milestones - so this edge describes a variably expressed consequence, not a constant one.

edges/14.description: The morphological finding itself, as seen on the peripheral blood smear.

edges/15.description: A candidate route, not a demonstrated one, and the entry should not be read as claiming otherwise. Urinary calcium excess causing parenchymal calcium deposition is ordinary renal physiology and is why the first-report authors screened hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis genes as one panel. But in this family the order of observation runs the wrong way for a simple causal story: proband II(1) had nephrocalcinosis on ultrasound in the newborn period and his hypercalciuria was documented at age 4, and proband II(2) had nephrocalcinosis from infancy with no hypercalciuria reported at all. So the edge records the only intermediate the evidence offers, typed with unknown intermediates, and the direct edge from the upstream node is deliberately kept in parallel.

evidence.snippet: Exon 2 of AMMECR1 encodes a domain consisting of six amino acids identically conserved throughout the course of evolution and whose function is as yet unknown.
evidence.explanation: The deep conservation that made the gene a plausible candidate, together with the statement that its function was unknown - which has not since been resolved.

evidence.snippet: In these cases, AMMECR1 gene appears to be responsible for most of the clinical features of the AMME syndrome except for Alport syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease assignment stated exactly: AMMECR1 carries the AMME phenotype minus its renal component.

evidence.snippet: Additional cases and functional studies are needed to clarify genotype-phenotype correlations and underlying disease mechanisms.
evidence.explanation: The current state of the gene-disease relationship in its authors' words, and the reason this entry asserts no correlation between allele type and phenotype.

genes/0.notes:
Encodes a 35.5 kDa nuclear protein of six exons with a ubiquitous transcript, conserved from yeast and Caenorhabditis elegans upward, carrying a nucleic-acid-binding RAGNYA fold and dimerizing with its paralog AMMECR1L. It was cloned specifically because it lay inside the AMME deletion interval and was named after that syndrome; its function was unknown then and is still not established.
The gene's position is the whole story of this disease. It sits telomeric to COL4A5 in Xq22.3, inside the interval whose deletion produces AMME. Because COL4A5 accounts for the Alport syndrome and nothing else, the remaining features had to belong to a neighbour, and both point mutations and AMMECR1-sparing-COL4A5 microdeletions have since confirmed the assignment from opposite directions.
Allelic spectrum: microdeletions (including small ones covering only TMEM164, AMMECR1 and SNORD96B), nonsense variants, an X-autosome translocation with inactivation of the normal X, and at least two missense alleles - p.G177D and p.Val217Met - both associated with altered intranuclear distribution. No genotype-phenotype correlation has been established.

evidence.snippet: He had bilateral mixed hearing loss requiring hearing aids
evidence.explanation: The intervention as reported in proband II(1).

evidence.snippet: Both abnormalities were corrected (with hearing aids and cleft palate repair), which may explain the improvement in speech and language development.
evidence.explanation: The outcome the authors attribute to amplification and palate repair together. INDIRECT because it is an uncontrolled single-family observation and the source hedges it - "may explain" - and because the two interventions are not separable in it.

treatments/0.description:
Amplification for the sensorineural hearing loss. In the first point-mutation family the older half-brother had bilateral mixed hearing loss requiring hearing aids, and the authors attribute part of his subsequent speech and language improvement to the correction of his hearing and palate together.
This is phenotype-directed and not disease-modifying, which is the only kind of treatment this entity has: nothing is known about what AMMECR1 does, so there is no mechanism to aim at. Because the loss is progressive rather than static, the clinical decision is not a one-off fitting but repeat audiometry with amplification adjusted as thresholds move - see the Audiometry entry under `diagnosis`.

evidence.snippet: He had surgical correction for a submucous cleft palate and bifid uvula.
evidence.explanation: The procedure as reported in proband II(1).

evidence.snippet: He was discharged from physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech and language therapy before his second birthday, having made improvements in his gross motor development and feeding following cleft palate repair.
evidence.explanation: The reported outcome. INDIRECT: an uncontrolled observation in one child, with the developmental improvement temporally associated with the repair rather than shown to follow from it.

treatments/1.description: Surgical closure of the submucous cleft palate and bifid uvula. Both point-mutation half-brothers had the palatal defect and the older one underwent surgical correction; his feeding and gross motor development improved afterwards, and the authors name the repair as one of two corrections that may account for his speech and language gains.

evidence.snippet: He had congenital dysplasia of the hips treated with a Pavlik harness.
evidence.explanation: The intervention as reported in proband II(2).

treatments/2.description: Abduction bracing for the congenital hip dysplasia, applied in proband II(2). Curated because hip dysplasia is one of this entry's phenotypes and this is the only management of it any source reports; no outcome is given.

open_questions/0.rationale: Twenty-seven years after the syndrome was described and twenty-six after the gene was cloned, the function of AMMECR1 is stated in the literature as unknown or, at its strongest, as "potentially involved in cell cycle control" on the basis of coexpression. There is no assay of AMMECR1 activity, no cell-cycle measurement in patient material, and no proposed route from the gene to any one of the four features in the disease name. This is not a gap in one branch of an otherwise worked-out mechanism - it is the whole mechanism, and the entry's causal edges are typed with unknown intermediates for that reason. The tractable next steps are the obvious ones: a conditional mouse or a patient-derived cell model with an actual readout, and a molecular function for the RAGNYA fold beyond the sequence prediction.

open_questions/1.rationale: Hereditary elliptocytosis is a disease of the spectrin-actin membrane skeleton, and the obvious hypothesis for an inherited elliptocytosis is that the same machinery is affected. That hypothesis was tested in the original AMME family and failed: red cell membrane proteins were normal and ektacytometry showed normal membrane stability and rigidity. So the morphology is produced some other way - plausibly during erythropoiesis rather than in the mature cell, given a nuclear protein with a proposed cell-cycle role - and nobody has looked. A negative result this clean, left unfollowed for a quarter century, is unusually good value for a small experiment.

open_questions/2.rationale: All three carrier females in the one report that examined them had hearing loss, and one had a cleft palate and hip dysplasia - and separately, one of the five patients in the loss-of-function series is a girl, affected because a balanced X-autosome translocation inactivated her normal X. So the "recessive" label is doing less work than it appears to. Three women is not a denominator, no other report audiometrically examines carriers, and the counselling consequence is direct: a carrier mother currently gets a recurrence risk without any statement of her own risk. Resolving it needs systematic audiometry in obligate carriers across the reported families, with X-inactivation studies alongside.

evidence.snippet: Screening of patient NDUFS2 cDNA by reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in combination with direct DNA sequencing revealed three missense mutations resulting in the substitution of conserved amino acids in three families.
evidence.explanation: The founding observation: three missense alleles at conserved residues in three families.

evidence.snippet: The interfacial region between these two arms is known to be critical for binding of ubiquinone moieties and has also been shown to be the binding site of Complex I inhibitors.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the functional significance of the region NDUFS2 occupies.

evidence.snippet: Ndufs2 makes up a significant part of the site of ubiquinone binding and is therefore essential for the enzymatic activity of mitochondrial complex I
evidence.explanation: States why this subunit is catalytically essential rather than structural scaffolding.

evidence.snippet: Global deletion of Ndufs2 is embryonic lethal
evidence.explanation: Establishes that complete loss is not compatible with development in mouse, which is consistent with human disease alleles being missense rather than truncating.

steps/1.description:
NDUFS2 encodes the 49 kDa subunit, one of the fourteen core subunits required for catalysis rather than one of the accessory subunits. It is a peripheral-arm subunit sitting at the interface between the membrane and matrix arms of the enzyme, the region that binds ubiquinone and that is also where complex I inhibitors bind.
The reported disease alleles are missense changes at conserved residues. The original report found three, in three families, identified by sequencing NDUFS2 complementary DNA in enzymatically complex I-deficient patients. Later reports include compound heterozygous and homozygous alleles, and at least one patient carried heterozygous changes in both NDUFA8 and NDUFS2, which the reporting authors flagged as raising the possibility of unconventional inheritance in complex I defects rather than as an established digenic mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that mutations of this arginine residue (R121M/K) abolish the quinone-reductase activity, concomitant with disappearance of the N2 signature from the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrum.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that a single conserved residue in this subunit controls both the presence of the cluster and the enzyme's catalytic output.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of the cryo-EM structure of NDUFS2-R121M complex I at 3.7 Å resolution identified the absence of the cubane N2 cluster as the cause of the dysfunction, within an otherwise intact enzyme.
evidence.explanation: The structural demonstration that catalysis can fail in a particle that did assemble. Read together with the content measurements below, it licenses "an assembled particle can be dead", not "the amount is normal".

evidence.snippet: although it is clear that mutations of R121 impair the assembly and/or stability of complex I, a level of intact enzyme is still present and available for study
evidence.explanation: The correction to any reading of this node as a pure catalytic lesion. The residue impairs assembly and stability as well; what the structural work established is that enough intact enzyme remains to be studied, and that the enzyme which remains cannot reduce quinone.

evidence.snippet: The mutation further induced localized disorder in nearby elements of the quinone-binding site, consistent with the close connections between the cluster and substrate-binding regions.
evidence.explanation: Shows the lesion extends from the cluster into the substrate-binding site, compounding the catalytic defect.

evidence.snippet: referred to as cluster N2 that is located at the interface of the NDUFS2 (NUCM) and NDUFS7 (NUKM) subunits
evidence.explanation: Places the cluster at the interface between the two subunits, which is the structural fact behind this node.

evidence.snippet: Cluster N2 is positioned ∼12 Å above the quinone-binding site and ligated by four cysteine residues in NDUFS7
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the cluster's direct ligands are in NDUFS7, not NDUFS2. This is what makes the NDUFS2 contribution a second-coordination-sphere effect and explains how an NDUFS2 residue can abolish a cluster it does not hold.

evidence.snippet: They contain no FeS clusters, but NDUFS2 forms part of the ubiquinone binding site.
evidence.explanation: Consistent with the interface reading rather than in conflict with it: the NDUFS2 region holds no cluster of its own, and NDUFS2's contribution is the quinone-binding site plus the second coordination sphere of a cluster ligated by NDUFS7.

steps/2.description:
The catalytic arm of the lesion, and the more precisely characterised of the two. N2 is the last iron-sulfur cluster in the electron relay and the one that reduces ubiquinone. It sits at the NDUFS2-NDUFS7 interface, ligated by four cysteines in NDUFS7 and positioned about 12 angstroms above the quinone-binding site, with NDUFS2 residues forming its second coordination sphere. NDUFS2 therefore controls the cluster without holding it, which is what makes an NDUFS2 defect able to remove it. A conserved arginine near the cluster, which is post-translationally dimethylated, turns out to be required for the cluster to form or to remain stable: substituting it abolishes quinone-reductase activity, the N2 signature disappears from the electron paramagnetic resonance spectrum, and cryo-electron microscopy shows the cubane cluster simply absent from an otherwise intact enzyme. The same substitution also disorders nearby elements of the quinone-binding site.
That last point is what makes this node worth separating from the assembly node, but the claim it licenses is narrower than it first appears. What the structure shows is that a particle which does assemble can be structurally native-like and catalytically dead. It does not show that the amount of enzyme is normal: in the same experiments, complex I content fell to about 40 percent and 25 percent of wild type for the two substitutions, and the authors state plainly that mutations of this residue impair assembly and stability as well. R121 is therefore a residue that hits both arms of this entry at once, which is consistent with the allele-dependent picture rather than an exception to it.

evidence.snippet: Some mutants were also analyzed using recently developed assays of assembly, time-delayed expression, and co-immunoprecipitation, which showed that assembly was disrupted.
evidence.explanation: The direct test of the assembly hypothesis, in the bacterial model system.

evidence.snippet: This indicates the possibility of a severe assembly defect with NDUFS2_ R228Q under normal expression in humans. In addition, E. coli modeled NDUFS2_ R138Q and Y141C appear to have greatly diminished activity, even when assembled normally.
evidence.explanation: The per-allele result that separates the two arms: R228Q is an assembly lesion, R138Q and Y141C are catalytic lesions in a normally assembled enzyme.

evidence.snippet: dNADH:APAD+ activity indicated that the complex I contents were ∼40% and 25% for R121M and R121K, respectively, relative to wild-type, corroborating the observations from BN-PAGE.
evidence.explanation: A second and independent line of support for this node, and in a eukaryotic enzyme rather than a bacterial one, which speaks directly to the reason this node is PROVISIONAL. Substituting a single NDUFS2 residue reduces the amount of assembled complex I by 60 to 75 percent.

evidence.snippet: arginine acts as part of a key/lock mechanism, helping to hold NDUFS2 and NDUFS7 together at a crucial point in the assembly process
evidence.explanation: Proposes the mechanism by which an NDUFS2 residue governs assembly, which gives this node a molecular account rather than only an observation that interface variants disrupt assembly.

evidence.snippet: The mutations were constructed in the homologous E. coli genes, nuoG, nuoCD, nuoI and nuoF, respectively, and expressed from a plasmid containing all Complex I genes.
evidence.explanation: The reason this node is PROVISIONAL: the assembly evidence comes from a homologous bacterial enzyme rather than from the human complex.

steps/3.description:
The second, structural arm. Complex I has 45 subunits, seven encoded in mitochondrial DNA and 38 imported, and many of the disease variants reported across its peripheral core subunits fall at subunit interfaces. Modelling seventeen human variant positions as thirty-one mutants in the homologous Escherichia coli enzyme produced a range of reduced activity, and assembly assays, time-delayed expression and co-immunoprecipitation showed that assembly was disrupted.
The per-allele results are what make this node useful rather than generic, and they split the NDUFS2 alleles in two. Modelled R228Q showed a severe assembly defect: NuoCD and NuoI were no longer co-immunoprecipitated with NuoG. Modelled R138Q and Y141C did the opposite, retaining greatly diminished activity even when assembled normally. So the same subunit produces assembly lesions and catalytic lesions depending on which residue is hit, and the two arms of this entry are allele-dependent rather than competing accounts of one lesion.
What keeps this PROVISIONAL is the system rather than the specificity. The work was done in a homologous bacterial enzyme, with human residues mapped onto their E. coli equivalents, so the assembly pathway is analogous rather than identical and the human consequence is inferred.

evidence.snippet: Disruption of NDUFS2 significantly decreased cell growth in medium, Complex I specific respiration, glycolytic capacity, ATP pool and cell-membrane integrity, but significantly increased Complex II respiration, ROS generation, apoptosis, and necrosis.
evidence.explanation: Measures every component of this node in one experiment, including the compensatory rise in complex II respiration.

evidence.snippet: ndufs2 -/- zebrafish had 80% reduced CI enzyme activity. Unbiased metabolomic profiling showed increased lactate, TCA cycle intermediates, and acyl-carnitine species.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the enzymatic deficit in vivo and shows the metabolic consequences propagating beyond oxidative phosphorylation.

steps/4.description:
The cellular endpoint, and it is not only an energy deficit. A CRISPR knockout of NDUFS2 in human embryonic kidney cells reduces growth, complex I-specific respiration, glycolytic capacity, ATP pool and membrane integrity, while increasing reactive oxygen species production, apoptosis and necrosis. Complex II respiration rises, which is the expected compensatory shift when the complex I entry point to the chain is blocked and complex II is intact.
In an ndufs2 knockout zebrafish, complex I enzyme activity falls by 80 percent and unbiased metabolomics shows raised lactate, raised tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates and raised acylcarnitines, so the block propagates into fatty acid oxidation and the cycle as well as into oxidative phosphorylation.

evidence.snippet: Neonatal presentation can be fatal with neuromuscular dysfunction, lactic acidosis and hepatic failure.
evidence.explanation: States the triad of the fatal neonatal presentation, in the report of a patient with confirmed biallelic NDUFS2 variants.

evidence.snippet: Similar transcriptomic profiles were observed in ndufs2 -/- missense mutant C. elegans (gas-1(fc21)) and two human CI-disease fibroblast cell lines stressed in galactose media.
evidence.explanation: Shows the metabolic signature is conserved across two model organisms and human patient cells, which is what makes it more than a zebrafish finding.

steps/5.description: The systemic expression of the block. Lactic acidosis is one of the three features that define the fatal neonatal presentation of mitochondrial disease, alongside neuromuscular dysfunction and hepatic failure. In the zebrafish knockout the same metabolic picture appears with an addition worth noting: one-carbon metabolism is dysregulated, and the same signature was seen in a missense ndufs2 mutant nematode and in two human complex I-deficient fibroblast lines stressed in galactose, so it is not an artefact of one species.

evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) deficiency represents a common biochemical pathophysiology underlying Leigh syndrome spectrum (LSS), manifesting with progressive multi-system dysfunction, lactic acidemia, and early mortality.
evidence.explanation: States the relationship between the biochemical lesion and the clinical syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Using massive parallel sequencing we were able to detect pathogenic variants in other 16 LS nuclear genes: NDUFV1, NDUFS2, NDUFS8, NDUFAF5, NDUFAF6, NDUFA10, SUCLG1, GFM2, COX10, PMPCB, NARS2, PDHB, SLC19A3 and IARS2
evidence.explanation: Places NDUFS2 among the nuclear genes causing Leigh syndrome in a national patient cohort.

steps/6.description: The commonest destination. Complex I deficiency is the commonest biochemical cause of the Leigh syndrome spectrum, and NDUFS2 appears among the nuclear Leigh genes detected by sequencing in national cohorts. Progressive leukoencephalopathy is a separate presentation within the same clinical range, and unspecified encephalomyopathy a third.

evidence.snippet: We analyzed the entire mtDNA and 11 nuclear encoded complex I subunits in 23 isolated complex I-deficient children, classified into five clinical groups: Leigh syndrome, progressive leukoencephalopathy, neonatal cardiomyopathy, severe infantile lactic acidosis, and a miscellaneous group of unspecified encephalomyopathies.
evidence.explanation: Establishes neonatal cardiomyopathy as a recognised clinical group within childhood complex I deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the nuclearly-encoded subunits have been regularly discovered in humans in recent years, and many lead to cardiomyopathy, Leigh Syndrome, and early death.
evidence.explanation: Records cardiomyopathy as one of the recognised outcomes of nuclear complex I subunit variants.

steps/7.description: Cardiomyopathy was part of the clinical description in which NDUFS2 was first implicated, and neonatal cardiomyopathy is one of the five recognised clinical groups of childhood complex I deficiency. It is not universal, and which patients develop it is not predictable from the genotype on current evidence.

evidence.snippet: Postmortem hepatocyte hypereosinophilia with microvesicular steatosis associated with ultrastructural findings of mitochondrial hyperplasia supported a mitochondriopathy.
evidence.explanation: The characterised hepatic morphology in a patient with biallelic NDUFS2 variants.

evidence.snippet: Morphologic attributes can assist in diagnosis of mitochondriopathies before specific genetic testing results are available.
evidence.explanation: The diagnostic point the reporting authors draw from the case.

steps/8.description:
Liver disease is part of the fatal neonatal presentation and has a characterised morphology: hepatocyte hypereosinophilia with microvesicular steatosis, and mitochondrial hyperplasia on ultrastructural examination. The reporting authors make a practical point about it, which is that the morphology supported the diagnosis before the genetic testing returned. Hepatomegaly is also present in the ndufs2 knockout zebrafish and is one of the two phenotypes rescued by folic acid there.
PROVISIONAL because the human evidence is a single autopsy case, and the frequency of hepatic involvement across NDUFS2 patients is not established.

evidence.snippet: The cofactor that transfers the electrons directly to ubiquinone is an iron-sulfur cluster (N2) located in the NDUFS2/NUCM subunit.
evidence.explanation: Locates the terminal electron-transfer cluster in the subunit this disease affects.

edges/1.description: NDUFS2 carries the terminal iron-sulfur cluster of the electron relay, so variants affecting its coordination remove the step that delivers electrons to ubiquinone.

evidence.snippet: Many of these mutations, found in NDUFS1, NDUFS2, NDUFS8, and NDUFV1, map to subunit interfaces, and we hypothesized that they would disrupt assembly of Complex I.
evidence.explanation: States the structural rationale for the assembly arm, in the study that went on to test it.

edges/2.description: Disease variants at subunit interfaces prevent the holoenzyme from assembling correctly, a separate consequence from loss of catalysis.

evidence.snippet: Disruption of NDUFS2 significantly decreased cell growth in medium, Complex I specific respiration, glycolytic capacity, ATP pool and cell-membrane integrity
evidence.explanation: Measures the bioenergetic consequence of losing the subunit in a knockout cell line.

edges/3.description: An enzyme that cannot reduce ubiquinone cannot support electron transport through complex I, whatever its abundance.

evidence.snippet: Membrane vesicles were prepared and rates of deamino-NADH oxidase activity measured, which indicated a range of reduced activity.
evidence.explanation: Links the interface variants to a measured reduction in enzyme activity.

edges/4.description: An enzyme that does not assemble cannot function, independently of whether its catalytic centre is intact.

evidence.snippet: Unbiased metabolomic profiling showed increased lactate, TCA cycle intermediates, and acyl-carnitine species.
evidence.explanation: Shows lactate accumulation as a direct metabolic consequence of the enzymatic deficit.

edges/5.description: Failure of oxidative phosphorylation forces reliance on glycolysis and accumulates the intermediates that cannot be oxidised.

evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) deficiency represents a common biochemical pathophysiology underlying Leigh syndrome spectrum (LSS), manifesting with progressive multi-system dysfunction, lactic acidemia, and early mortality.
evidence.explanation: States the causal relationship between complex I deficiency and the Leigh syndrome spectrum.

edges/6.description: The central nervous system is the tissue least able to tolerate an oxidative phosphorylation deficit.

evidence.snippet: We analyzed the entire mtDNA and 11 nuclear encoded complex I subunits in 23 isolated complex I-deficient children, classified into five clinical groups: Leigh syndrome, progressive leukoencephalopathy, neonatal cardiomyopathy, severe infantile lactic acidosis, and a miscellaneous group of unspecified encephalomyopathies.
evidence.explanation: Establishes neonatal cardiomyopathy as one of the five clinical groups into which complex I deficiency in children falls.

edges/7.description: Cardiac muscle is the other tissue with an oxidative phosphorylation demand it cannot meet by glycolysis, and cardiomyopathy was part of the presentation in which this gene was first implicated.

evidence.snippet: Postmortem hepatocyte hypereosinophilia with microvesicular steatosis associated with ultrastructural findings of mitochondrial hyperplasia supported a mitochondriopathy.
evidence.explanation: Documents the hepatic tissue changes in a patient with biallelic NDUFS2 variants.

edges/8.description: Hepatic failure is part of the fatal neonatal triad, and postmortem examination shows the hepatocyte and mitochondrial changes underlying it.

evidence.snippet: The NDUFS2 protein is part of complex I of many pro- and eukaryotes. The nuclear gene coding for this protein is therefore an important candidate for mutational detection studies in enzymatic complex I deficient patients.
evidence.explanation: States the conservation argument that made this gene a candidate.

evidence.snippet: A genetic definition was reached in eight patients (35%).
evidence.explanation: Bounds how much of childhood complex I deficiency any single subunit gene explains: in this cohort most patients had no genetic diagnosis at all.

evidence.snippet: The latter cases suggest the possibility of unconventional patterns of inheritance in complex I defects.
evidence.explanation: The reporting authors' own framing of the NDUFA8-plus-NDUFS2 patient, as a possibility raised rather than a mechanism shown.

genes/0.notes:
NDUFS2 encodes the 49 kDa core subunit of complex I, one of the fourteen subunits required for catalysis. Reported disease alleles are missense changes at conserved residues; the founding report described three, in three families. Because complex I has 45 subunits and at least eight nuclear-encoded ones were already implicated by 2004, NDUFS2 accounts for a small share of childhood complex I deficiency, and in the cohort that first surveyed the genetics only 35 percent of patients reached a genetic diagnosis at all.
One reported patient carried heterozygous changes in both NDUFA8 and NDUFS2. The reporting authors raised that as a possible unconventional pattern of inheritance rather than as a demonstrated digenic mechanism, and it is recorded here the same way.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with idebenone, a clinical benzoquinone currently being investigated in other indications, partially restored growth, ATP pool, and oxygen consumption of the mutant.
evidence.explanation: Cited here to substantiate why this entry curates supportive care and nothing disease-directed, not to support supportive care itself. The strongest therapeutic signal that exists for this gene was obtained in a cell line, which is the reason there is no disease-directed treatment to curate. The same result is recorded where it belongs mechanistically, as a RESTORED readout on the knockout cell line under experimental_models.

treatments/0.description:
There is no disease-modifying therapy and no NDUFS2-directed treatment. Management is supportive and follows the organ involvement: seizure control, nutritional and feeding support, cardiac and hepatic monitoring, and developmental therapies. Nothing in this is specific to NDUFS2 and none of it has been evaluated in this disorder.
Two preclinical leads exist and are deliberately not curated as treatments, because neither has been given to a patient with this disorder. open_questions/0.rationale:
Two routes from an NDUFS2 variant to complex I failure are separately documented, and they are not the same kind of defect. The catalytic route is the more precisely characterised: substituting a conserved arginine near the N2 cluster abolishes quinone-reductase activity and removes the cluster from an enzyme that cryo-electron microscopy shows to be otherwise intact. The assembly route comes from mapping human variants onto subunit interfaces and reproducing them in a bacterial enzyme, where assembly assays showed disruption.
The two make different predictions about what a diagnostic assay would find, though not cleanly opposite ones. A predominantly catalytic lesion depresses activity more than amount, so the ratio of activity to assembled enzyme falls below one while blue native gel electrophoresis may look close to normal. A predominantly assembly lesion depresses both roughly together, so the ratio is preserved while the amount falls. What distinguishes them is therefore the ratio rather than either measurement alone, which is why the experiment proposed below measures both in the same cells.
The distinction has already been drawn for individual alleles, and the answer differs between them. In the bacterial model, R228Q showed a severe assembly defect while R138Q and Y141C retained greatly diminished activity even when assembled normally. In patient material, the fibroblasts of the R138Q/R333Q compound heterozygote had complex I activity low and assembly at about 50 percent of normal, so that patient had both. What is missing is not the concept but the series: no study has measured amount and activity together across the reported NDUFS2 alleles in patient material under one protocol, and the two existing sources use different systems and different alleles.
Two caveats bound the available evidence. The per-allele assembly results were generated in a homologous bacterial enzyme rather than the human complex, so the human consequence is inferred from an analogous system. And the catalytic evidence from structural work has two limits. R121 is a conserved residue investigated for its post-translational methylation rather than a reported patient allele, so it demonstrates what the region does without being a disease variant itself. And it is not a clean catalytic-only exemplar: its substitutions reduce complex I content to 40 and 25 percent of wild type and reduce membrane enrichment by 60 to 75 percent, and the authors propose the residue acts as part of a key-and-lock holding NDUFS2 and NDUFS7 together during assembly. R121 therefore illustrates the catalytic arm and belongs to the assembly arm at the same time.

open_questions/1.rationale:
Anyone reading the mouse literature on complex I deficiency will mostly be reading about Ndufs4, which is the standard model for Leigh syndrome and which has been characterised in far more detail than Ndufs2. The two genes are not interchangeable, and the difference is exactly the distinction this entry's two mechanistic nodes turn on. Ndufs2 is a core catalytic subunit that forms a substantial part of the ubiquinone-binding site and is essential for enzymatic activity. Ndufs4 is an 18 kDa accessory subunit that does not participate in electron transfer at all and is instead thought to act as an assembly factor contributing to the stability of the assembled complex.
The severity difference follows from that and is stark: global deletion of Ndufs2 is embryonic lethal, whereas global loss of Ndufs4 is compatible with about two months of life in most models. A therapeutic tested successfully in Ndufs4 mice has been tested against an assembly and stability defect with a partially functional enzyme, not against an enzyme that cannot reduce ubiquinone.
There is one point of genuine convergence worth recording, because it suggests where a shared therapeutic strategy might survive the substitution. Expressing the yeast alternative NADH dehydrogenase NDI1, which oxidises NADH independently of complex I, extended lifespan in brain-specific Ndufs2 knockouts just as it had in Ndufs4 mice. That is a result about restoring NADH oxidation, which both defects lose, rather than about repairing either protein.
What is missing is a mouse model of the actual human genotype. Every Ndufs2 mouse described here is either a heterozygous deletion, which produces no phenotype, or a complete knockout, which is lethal. Human patients carry biallelic missense alleles with residual function, and no model occupies that middle ground.

evidence.explanation: Confirms fasting and illness as triggers for metabolic crises, supporting avoidance strategy.

treatments/3.description: Preventing prolonged fasting is critical. Frequent meals, cornstarch supplementation at night, and emergency protocols with IV glucose during illness help prevent metabolic decompensation.

evidence.snippet: Therapy is similar to VLCAD deficiency and includes avoiding the physiologic triggers of fasting and illness.
evidence.explanation: Review guidance supports avoiding fasting and illness triggers to reduce catabolic energy stress.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Avoiding fasting and illness-triggered catabolism reduces episodes when impaired FAO cannot meet energy demand.

evidence.snippet: Carnitine supplementation remains controversial, but low doses do not cause harm. Intravenous supplementation of carnitine in high doses during decompensation is not recommended.
evidence.explanation: Supports a cautious carnitine entry while preventing overstatement of routine high-dose use.

treatments/4.description: Low-dose L-carnitine is a controversial supportive option in MTP deficiency, and high-dose intravenous carnitine during decompensation is not recommended.

evidence.snippet: Carnitine supplementation remains controversial, but low doses do not cause harm.
evidence.explanation: Review guidance supports only a cautious, low-dose role for carnitine in TFP deficiency.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Low-dose carnitine is a conditional supportive intervention rather than correction of the TFP enzyme block.

evidence.snippet: MTP is pharmacologically up-regulated by bezafibrate in human fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Confirms pharmacological upregulation of MTP by bezafibrate.

treatments/5.description: Bezafibrate, a PPAR-alpha agonist, has been shown to upregulate MTP expression in control fibroblasts and improve fatty acid oxidation capacities in a subset (23%) of MTP-deficient patient cell lines, particularly those heterozygous for the common c.1528G>C mutation.

evidence.snippet: activities of LCHAD and LCKAT, and stimulated FAO capacities, clearly indicating that MTP is pharmacologically up-regulated by bezafibrate in human fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Human fibroblast evidence supports bezafibrate as a pharmacologic modulator of residual MTP function.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Bezafibrate can upregulate HADHA/HADHB expression and residual MTP activity in responsive fibroblast genotypes.

evidence.snippet: Included studies suggested fewer heart and liver problems in screen-detected patients, but inconsistent results for mortality.
evidence.explanation: Supports newborn screening benefit for reducing cardiac and hepatic complications.

evidence.snippet: The mitigated phenotypes of this treatable disease were missed by the newborn screening, highlighting the importance of phenotype-based NGS analysis
evidence.explanation: Notes that milder MTP phenotypes may be missed by standard newborn screening.

treatments/6.description: MTP deficiency can be detected by newborn screening using tandem mass spectrometry to identify elevated long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines. Screen detection may be associated with fewer cardiac and hepatic complications, though mitigated phenotypes can be missed by screening.

evidence.snippet: Maternal hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelet count syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy were noted in two and one mothers, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Maternal complications necessitate genetic counseling and pregnancy monitoring.

evidence.snippet: Using amniotic fluid prenatal diagnostic testing, the unborn child was confirmed to carry only c.2107G>A (p.G703R).
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates availability and utility of prenatal diagnosis for MTP deficiency.

treatments/7.description: Genetic counseling for affected families including discussion of autosomal recessive inheritance, 25% recurrence risk, carrier testing, and prenatal diagnosis options. Maternal complications including HELLP syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy may occur in pregnancies carrying affected fetuses.
